T: Just the facts. And the food.
D: A by-the-book cop and his slacker partner take on a cult in LA.
P: Serve dinner when Friday and Streebek go undercover at the PAGAN ceremony.
S: Button mushrooms filled with cream cheese, garlic, parmesan and herbed breadcrumbs, baked until bubbling and golden on top. Heat the oven to 200C. Pull the stalks from 20 button mushrooms and chop them finely. Mix the stalks with 150g softened cream cheese, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 40g grated parmesan and chopped parsley. Fill each mushroom cap. Mix 30g breadcrumbs with 1 tbsp melted butter and press on top. Bake 15 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Friday's desk, all strictly by the book

Yeasted doughnut holes fried golden and fluffy, dipped warm in a thin vanilla glaze that sets glossy, served in neat rows on a plain plate. Warm 180ml milk with 30g butter and 2 tbsp caster sugar, add 7g yeast and 1 egg, then mix into 350g plain flour with a pinch of salt. Knead 5 minutes and prove 1 hour. Roll into 30 small balls and prove 20 minutes. Fry at 175C for 2 minutes, turning, until golden. Whisk 200g icing sugar with 3 tbsp milk and 1 tsp vanilla, dip the warm doughnuts and set on a rack.

Beef smashed thin on a smoking griddle, cheddar melted under a lid, with pickles, mustard and a slick of burger sauce on soft slider buns. Divide 500g beef mince into 12 balls. Heat a griddle or heavy pan until smoking. Smash each ball flat with a spatula, season and cook 2 minutes until crusty. Flip, add a quarter slice of cheddar, splash in a little water and cover for 30 seconds. Mix 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp tomato sauce and 1 tbsp chopped pickles for sauce. Toast 12 slider buns and fill with sauce, patty, pickles and mustard.
M: Friday's LA diner meatloaf and gravy

Beef and pork meatloaf with a tangy tomato glaze, cut into thick slices over creamy mash and smothered in rich brown onion gravy. Mix 500g beef mince, 300g pork mince, 60g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1 grated onion, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and salt. Shape in a lined loaf tin, spread with 80ml tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar and bake at 180C for 1 hour. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml hot milk. Fry 1 sliced onion in butter until brown, stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 350ml beef stock and simmer until thick.
Slow-braised pork shoulder crisped in the pan, in warm tortillas with onion, coriander and lime.
W: Thick vanilla custard set between two sheets of puff pastry, topped with plain white icing and cut into neat squares.
K: Just the facts cold brew tonic
Friday takes his coffee black, and nothing extra

Strong cold brew coffee poured over ice and topped with tonic water and a squeeze of orange, sharp, bitter and fizzing. The night before, stir 100g coarsely ground coffee into 800ml cold water in a jug, cover and leave in the fridge for 12 to 16 hours. Strain through a paper filter. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in 150ml tonic water each, then slowly pour 100ml cold brew over the top so it layers. Squeeze a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.

m.how: Cut 1.2kg pork shoulder into chunks, rub with cumin, oregano and salt and braise with 1 orange, 3 garlic cloves and 250ml water at 160C for 2.5 hours. Shred, crisp in the pan and serve in 16 corn tortillas with diced onion, coriander and lime.

w.how: Bake 2 sheets puff pastry pricked and weighted at 200C for 15 minutes. Whisk 1L milk, 6 egg yolks, 150g sugar, 90g cornflour and 2 tsp vanilla over medium heat until very thick. Spread between the pastry in a lined tin, chill 4 hours, ice with 200g icing sugar mixed with a little water and cut into squares.
